Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined pulse of AP-1-activating signal (e.g., TPA, TNF, or injury), let activity return to baseline, then re-stimulate days to weeks later. Compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq) and kinetics against naive cells to see whether prior exposure primes a faster or stronger response.

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag of AP-1 occupancy and chromatin accessibility
ideas.description: Profile AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding, motif accessibility, and histone marks (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) before, during, and long after stimulation. Persistent open or primed enhancers after AP-1 levels fall would indicate a chromatin-encoded memory footprint.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 loss-of-function with timed degradation
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) FOS or JUN, or dominant-negative A-FOS, to remove AP-1 either during the initial stimulus or only during the memory interval. This separates AP-1's role in establishing memory from maintaining it, and tests whether enhancer accessibility and the primed response are lost.

ideas.title: Live-cell single-cell reporters and lineage tracking
ideas.description: Image AP-1 activity with fluorescent reporters or tagged FOS/JUN in single cells after a pulse, following them and their daughters over several divisions. Test whether heterogeneous or persistent activity states are heritable and correlate with later response strength, distinguishing cell-intrinsic memory from ongoing signaling.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 site editing and in vivo injury model
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate or insert AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, and test the effect on primed responses in cells. Parallel in vivo repeat-injury or repeat-inflammation experiments, such as skin wounding, with AP-1 perturbation would test whether memory is functionally relevant in tissue.
